record_group: RG-02-001 Office of the President records
departmental_identity: Department of Philosophy and Psychology / later Philosophy Psychology and Education context
evidence_basis: Published archival scholarship on James Mark Baldwin cites Records of the Office of the President RG 02.001 Series 1 File No. 56 Department of Philosophy and Psychology; current JHU authority history independently confirms the combined department existed 1903-1908 and expanded to Philosophy Psychology and Education 1908-1915
retrieval_implication: Establishes that RG-02-001 Series 1 used numbered departmental subject files for philosophy/psychology administration before the 1915 split; use as a structural precedent when asking for post-1915 Philosophy files
prohibited_inference: Do not project File 56 forward to 1916 or claim that Lovejoy/Russell material is in File 56
notes: The published File 56 citation is secondary-exact; the departmental chronology is current primary authority description.

record_group: RG-02-001 Office of the President records
evidence_basis: Published archival research on John B. Watson gives exact Hamburger-Archives citations to RG 02.001 / Office of the President / Series 1 / File 115 Department of Psychology 1913-1919 and 1920-1921
retrieval_implication: Demonstrates that the same presidential Series 1 continued to preserve a distinct departmental subject file after the 1915 separation; strengthens the expectation that Philosophy may likewise have had a separate Series 1 file, but its number remains unknown
prohibited_inference: Do not infer that Philosophy shared File 115 or that the Russell packet is physically adjacent to Watson material
notes: The post-split file architecture is evidenced for Psychology only.

legacy_file_or_domain: post-1915 Department of Philosophy file; exact file number unresolved
departmental_identity: Johns Hopkins University Department of Philosophy
evidence_basis: Current JHU authority record says Philosophy Psychology and Education formally split into separate departments around 1915; current Philosophy finding aid says they were formally divided into three seminaries in 1915-1916 and Lovejoy was Professor of Philosophy from 1910
relation_to_GLA0030: Canonical GLA0030 is a Lovejoy / Department of Philosophy document in the historical University Archives concerning a Bertrand Russell lecture, probably 1916-17 episode
retrieval_implication: Request RG-02-001 Series 1 Department of Philosophy files covering 1915-1917 by department title and date before relying on personal-name indexing; search Lovejoy Russell lecture visiting appointment technical philosophy war/pacifism within the recovered file
prohibited_inference: Do not assign an invented file number, recipient, date, or box; the existence of analogous File 56 and File 115 does not prove a specific Philosophy file survives
notes: This is now a bounded series-and-department retrieval target rather than a generic RG-02-001 search.

retrieval_implication: Use RG-04-120 for later copies or retrospective references only after RG-02-001/other 1916 administrative domains are exhausted

notes: The historical department predates the current record group's holdings.
